rules.canonical:
You are one of two cogs carrying a couch through a warehouse obstacle course.
You and your partner are gripped to opposite ends of the same rigid couch: you
hold one handle, your partner holds the other. The couch moves according to the
SUM of the two forces you apply, and it TURNS according to the difference. If you
both push the same way it slides; if you disagree it spins into a wall.
THERE IS NO COMMUNICATION CHANNEL. You cannot talk to your partner and your
partner never sees anything you write. The only information you get about your
partner is the force you feel through your own handle ("strain") and where their
end of the couch is. Read the strain: it tells you whether to lead or to yield.
Every 2 seconds you set your carry parameters for the next 2 seconds. A
deterministic controller executes them at 24 Hz.
The couch is 2.20 m long and 0.90 m wide. Doorways are between 1.05 m and 2.20 m
wide; the last one is 1.05 m. Scraping a wall and slamming into one both damage
the couch; if the strain in your hands stays too high for too long you drop it,
which costs 2 seconds and a chunk of condition.
rules.plain:
You and one partner carry a rigid couch through a warehouse obstacle course, each holding the opposite handle. The sum of your forces moves the couch; their difference turns it. Pushing together slides it, while disagreement can spin it into a wall.
There is no communication channel. Your partner never sees your writing. You learn about them only from strain at your own handle and the position of their end of the couch. Read that strain to decide whether to lead or yield.
Choose carry parameters every 2 seconds; a deterministic controller applies them at 24 Hz for the following 2 seconds.
The couch measures 2.20 m by 0.90 m. Doorways range from 1.05 m to 2.20 m wide, with a 1.05 m final doorway. Scrapes and impacts damage the couch. Sustained excessive strain causes a drop, costing 2 seconds and condition.
rules.numbered:
1. Assignment: you are one of two cogs carrying a rigid couch through a warehouse course, holding opposite handles.
2. Motion: the sum of your forces translates the couch; their difference rotates it. Matching pushes slide it; disagreement can spin it into walls.
3. Privacy: there is no communication channel and your partner never sees your writing. Their only signals are strain in your own handle and their end's position. Use strain to choose between leading and yielding.
4. Timing: set carry parameters every 2 seconds for the next 2 seconds; execution is deterministic at 24 Hz.
5. Geometry: couch length 2.20 m, width 0.90 m; doorway widths 1.05–2.20 m; final doorway 1.05 m.
6. Damage: scraping or striking walls reduces condition. Excessive strain held too long drops the couch, losing 2 seconds and condition.
rules.questions:

rules.heldout-briefing:
Carry briefing: two cogs must move one rigid couch through a warehouse obstacle course. You grip one handle and your partner grips the opposite handle. Combined forces produce translation; their difference produces turning. Agreement slides the couch, while conflicting pushes can spin it into a wall.
Communications are unavailable: your partner cannot see anything you write. Read your own handle strain and the position of their end to decide when to lead or yield.
Issue carry parameters every 2 seconds. A deterministic 24 Hz controller executes each selection for the next 2 seconds.
Clearance: the couch is 2.20 m long and 0.90 m wide; doors are 1.05–2.20 m wide and the last is 1.05 m. Wall scrapes and impacts damage the couch. Prolonged overload at your handle causes a drop, with 2 seconds lost and condition damage.
rules.heldout-reference:
Team: two cogs gripping opposite handles of one rigid couch. Task: carry it through a warehouse obstacle course.
Translation: sum of both forces. Rotation: difference of forces. Aligned pushes slide the couch; conflicting pushes can spin it into a wall.
Partner information: position of their end and strain felt in your own handle only. Communication: none; your partner never sees your writing. Strategy: use strain to decide whether to lead or yield.
Parameter interval: every 2 seconds, lasting 2 seconds. Execution: deterministic controller at 24 Hz.
Couch dimensions: 2.20 m long by 0.90 m wide. Doorway widths: 1.05–2.20 m; final doorway: 1.05 m.
Condition losses: wall scrapes and impacts. Sustained excessive strain: couch drop, 2-second delay, and lost condition.

scoring: Both seats receive the same score. On delivery: 0.30 + 0.35 * speed + 0.35 * condition. Without delivery: 0.25 * progress * condition. Speed is clamp(2 - elapsed/par, 0, 1); condition is (1000 - damage)/1000. A wrecked couch scores zero.
response:
Reply with a single JSON object and NOTHING else. Your reply MUST begin with '{'.
Schema:
{"note":"<=160 chars",
 "drive":[x,y],    // direction to push, metres frame, each in [-1,1]; magnitude ignored
 "effort":0..1,    // how hard you push along drive (1 = your full 600 N)
 "yield":0..1,     // how much of the force you FEEL you push along with
                   // (1 = pure follower, 0 = ignore your partner completely)
 "twist":-1..1,    // rotate the couch: +1 counter-clockwise, -1 clockwise, 0 none
 "brace":0..1,     // plant your feet: halves your push, raises your grip limit
 "say":"<=48 chars"}   // spectators only; your partner NEVER sees this
